query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Addition of a refractory element improves elevated-temperature mechanical properties of titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloys
generation.intervention: Addition of a refractory element (e.g., tungsten or molybdenum) at 5-10 at%
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable, coherent precipitate phase
generation.mechanism: Precipitate strengthening and grain boundary pinning
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and creep resistance relative to the alloy without the refractory element addition
generation.baseline: Titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without refractory element addition
generation.boundary: Composition: 20-40 at% Ti, 20-40 at% Ni, 5-10 at% refractory element; Temperature: 500-1000°C; Stress: 100-500 MPa
generation.uncertainty: Effect of refractory element on alloy microstructure and properties, potential interactions with other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of yield strength and creep resistance between titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloys with and without refractory element addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with refractory element addition shows no significant improvement in yield strength or creep resistance compared to the alloy without refractory element addition, the hypothesis is falsified
